hypotheses.statement: Momentary emotion dysregulation mediates momentary associations between negative affect and loss-of-control (LOC) eating.
hypotheses.provenance_quote: The present study aimed to address these research gaps by examining: (1) whether emotion dysregulation mediated associations between negative and positive affect relative to LOC eating at the momentary level

hypotheses.provenance_quote: Also, all momentary mediational pathways involving positive affect as a predictor were not significant.

hypotheses.statement: These mediational associations vary across six distinct LOC eating dimensions.
hypotheses.provenance_quote: (2) variations in these associations across different LOC eating dimensions

hypotheses.statement: Reverse pathway: affect mediates associations between emotion dysregulation and LOC eating dimensions.

findings.quote: Participants responded to 3131 out of 4494 possible surveys, reflecting good compliance (70.00%).

consequence.explanation: Overstates EMA compliance by 0.33 percentage points; affects only the descriptive characterisation of compliance as 'good', not any inferential result.

findings.notes: TOOL ACTUALLY CALLED: check_count_percent (the `technique` enum has no entry for it; grim_percentage is the nearest registered percentage-check family, and check_count_percent is the strictly stronger version of it where the count is printed). The two counts are mutually consistent and independently verifiable: 6 surveys/day x 7 days x 107 participants = 4494, so the denominator is right. 3131/4494 = 69.67%, which the paper prints as 70.00% - rounded to a whole number but then formatted to two decimals, asserting a precision it does not have. Printing '69.67%' or '70%' would both have been accurate. Presentational defect, not a data-integrity one; nothing inferential depends on it.

consequence.explanation: The mediation effect for 'difficulties resisting eating' (p = .026) does not survive any of the four corrections, yet it is named in the abstract and conclusions as one of the dimensions emotion dysregulation was found to mediate. Computed from 1 result(s) significant uncorrected do not survive correction (a correction the paper did not apply, over a family we chose).

findings.notes: Twelve mediation tests on the same 107 participants, testing one hypothesis across six correlated outcomes, with no correction stated anywhere. Uncorrected testing is ordinary practice, not misconduct - but the arithmetic is that the family-wise error rate reaches 46% and about 0.6 false positives are expected by chance. Three of the four uncorrected claims are robust (all p = .001, surviving even Bonferroni); the fourth, difficulties resisting eating at p = .026, exceeds every threshold (Bonferroni .0042, BH .0125, BY .0040). Surviving-claims interval is 3 to 3 - all four methods agree. The six LOC outcomes are measured on the same subjects and are plainly correlated, so Benjamini-Yekutieli is the appropriate FDR method here, and it too keeps only 3.

findings.notes: This is the paper's key dimensional-variation claim and the weakest of its null results. The 95% interval derived from the printed b and SE runs to 0.099, LARGER than the mediation effects reported as significant for general LOC eating (b = 0.10), driven/compelled to eat (b = 0.09) and felt disconnected (b = 0.09). The data therefore do not distinguish this dimension from those; the paper is contrasting significant with non-significant rather than testing the difference between them. No SESOI is stated, so equivalence cannot be assessed and no 'no effect' conclusion is licensed. The interval is DERIVED, not printed - the paper reports no confidence intervals anywhere - and inherits the 2 dp rounding of b and SE.

consequence.explanation: The headline conclusion that positive-affect mediation was uniformly absent is carried by three marginal results (p = .065, .067, .070), not by clearly null ones - a weaker basis than the flat statement suggests.

findings.notes: READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE USING THIS. The derived interval excludes zero, which superficially contradicts the reported p = .065 - but that is a ROUNDING ARTIFACT, not a defect in the paper. b and SE are printed to 2 dp, so b = -0.02, SE = 0.01 taken at their midpoints gives z = -2.0; the true unrounded values (e.g. b = -0.018, SE = 0.0098) reconcile with p = .065 comfortably. check_regression_batch confirmed this row consistent, with a reachable p-interval of [6e-07, 0.317]. There is therefore NO internal contradiction, and none should be reported. The reportable observation is softer: three of the six within-person positive-affect mediation paths sit at p = .065-.070, all just above threshold, so the flat conclusion that positive-affect pathways 'were not significant' rests on marginal rather than clearly null evidence - and no confidence intervals are printed anywhere that would let a reader see this.

consequence.explanation: No APA-format test statistics appear in prose, so statcheck's p-recalculation could not apply anywhere; all inferential verification had to come from Table 2 instead.

findings.notes: A genuine zero, not a tool failure (statcheck returned success: true). The paper reports no t, F, chi-squared or z statistics with degrees of freedom in its narrative - all inference is presented as b (SE) and p in Table 2, which statcheck cannot see. This is why check_regression_batch carried the inferential verification for this paper. Recorded so the absence is not mistaken for 'nothing was checked'.

source.source_quote: Characteristics for the present sample (N = 107) are reported in Table 1. Participants responded to 3131 out of 4494 possible surveys, reflecting good compliance (70.00%).

findings.location: Participants and Procedures, second paragraph, first sentence

consequence.explanation: The trial registration cannot be looked up as printed, so a reader cannot check the parent trial's registered design or outcomes against this secondary analysis.

findings.notes: ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers are 'NCT' followed by exactly eight digits; the printed 'NCT0204349' has seven and does not resolve. The same malformed string appears in BOTH the XML and the PDF, so it is the paper's, not an extraction artifact. This is a typo in a load-bearing sentence - the registration is a reader's only route to the parent trial's protocol - which is why it is recorded rather than passed over. No claim is made about which digit is missing or what the correct identifier is; establishing that requires a registry lookup, outside this sweep. Recorded as `manual` because no forensic tool covers identifier format, and capped at `suspicious` accordingly.

findings.quote: (1) general feeling of losing control while eating (M = 2.26, SD = 1.32); (2) difficulties resisting eating (M = 2.79, SD = 1.42)

consequence.explanation: The six outcome variables' descriptive statistics cannot be granularity-checked at all, leaving the paper's only distributional summary of its outcomes unverifiable.

findings.notes: These are the ideal targets for GRIM/GRIMMER/SPRITE - single items on a STATED 1-5 integer scale - and all three are blocked for one reason: no denominator. The LOC items were shown only after a participant reported eating, so the relevant n is an unreported subset of the 3131 completed surveys, and neither the paper nor the available text gives it. Substituting 3131 would be inventing the denominator and could manufacture an impossibility, so nothing was run. Reported as a REPORTING gap: an EMA paper should state the number of eating-episode observations underlying its outcome descriptives. All six SDs (1.18-1.42) sit comfortably below the 2.0 half-range ceiling for a 1-5 scale, so nothing looks wrong; it simply cannot be checked.

findings.quote: overlaps with emotion dysregulation (r = .948 in the present study)

consequence.explanation: Bears on the paper's novelty claim relative to Wonderlich et al. (2024), which analysed the same sample using negative urgency as the mediator: at r = .948 the two mediators are close to interchangeable.

findings.notes: Not an arithmetic anomaly - r = .948 is well within bounds and no tool flags it. Recorded because the paper cites it in passing as evidence of 'overlap' when it in fact indicates the two constructs are barely distinguishable in this sample. The prior publication on this same dataset (Wonderlich et al. 2024) tested negative urgency as the mediator of the negative-affect-to-binge-eating path; the present paper tests emotion dysregulation. At this correlation those are close to the same analysis on the same participants, which is relevant to how independent the two sets of findings should be treated as being. No shared-variance figure is computed here, as that would be unaided arithmetic. Flagged for editorial judgement, not as a defect.

findings.location: Study Purpose, final paragraph (Stefano et al. citation)

consequence.explanation: A citation-year difference between the author manuscript and the version of record; no numeric or inferential claim depends on it.

findings.notes: The PDF is the PMC author manuscript and the XML the publisher version, so these are different versions of the same text and a copy-editing correction between them is the ordinary explanation. The XML uses 'Stefano et al. [2016]' consistently, including elsewhere on the same page; the PDF's single '2014' at this location appears to be the pre-correction reading. Recorded only so a reader working from the PDF is not confused. No accusation is implied.

source.source_quote: Note: N = 107; additional participant characteristics are reported in Peterson et al. ([2020]).

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Conceptual model depicting the associations of interest that were examined in the assessed multilevel structural equation models. i = individual; ED = emotion dysregulation; LOC = loss of control eating; NA = negative affect; PA = positive affect; t = time; negative affect and positive affect were predictors, the emotion dysregulation factors were mediators, and (in separate models) each LOC eating behavior was the outcome; to capture the temporal sequencing of the targeted associations and establish temporal precedence that is helpful to examine when mediational associations are assessed, indicators for the latent factors were lagged twice for the predictors (affect) and once for the mediators (emotion dysregulation).

panels.shows: Path diagram of the 1-1-1 mediation structure (affect at t-2 -> emotion dysregulation at t-1 -> LOC eating at t), showing which variables were lagged and at which level; it carries no estimated values.

tables_checked: Table 1 (Participant characteristics, 29 rows x 3 cols, 26 cells, 100% typed, 0 ambiguous)
Table 2 (MSEM results, 60 rows x 7 cols, 84 tests, 68 with exact p checked)

unchecked.location: Data S1 (Supporting Information) - multilevel CFA factor structures, all model fit indices, missing-data analyses, exploratory reverse-pathway MSEMs, and the comparison of excluded vs analytic participants
unchecked.reason: No supplementary file was among the inputs provided to this sweep (only the .xml and .pdf were supplied), so its contents could not be read. This is a substantial coverage gap, not a clean result: the supplement is where ALL model fit statistics live ('model fit statistics were good and are reported in Data S1'), where the entire exploratory analysis set is reported, and where the claim that the 5 excluded participants did not differ from the 107 analysed is substantiated. None of that could be verified. 'Present but not supplied to this review' is not the same as 'not provided by the authors'.

unchecked.location: Results, six LOC eating means and SDs (M = 2.26/2.79/2.54/2.88/3.45/2.19)
unchecked.reason: GRIM, GRIMMER and SPRITE all require an observation-level denominator and none is reported: the LOC items were administered only after a participant reported eating, so the relevant n is an unstated subset of the 3131 completed surveys. Substituting the survey total would be inventing the denominator. Recorded as finding loc_outcome_descriptives_no_denominator.

unchecked.location: Table 1, BDI / CIA / DERS total-score SDs (10.00, 9.87, 26.61)
unchecked.reason: check_table refused GRIMMER and SPRITE on these three rows because the paper states no scoring range for any of the three instruments. The tools would otherwise fall back to a default 1-7 Likert maximum, which for an unbounded total score manufactures an impossibility out of an ordinary value. The refusal is correct; a stated instrument range would make these checkable.

unchecked.location: Table 1, baseline age (39.87) and BMI (35.10) rows
unchecked.reason: Declared continuous, so the exact-arithmetic family (GRIM/GRIMMER/SPRITE) correctly does not apply. Age could in principle be integer-valued in whole years, but the paper does not say so; asserting it would be an assumed discreteness and could reach only `suspicious` in any case. check_sd_or_se ran on both and returned indeterminate, as no plausibility ceiling is stated for either variable.

unchecked.location: Table 2, the 16 coefficient rows whose p is printed as '< .001'
unchecked.reason: A thresholded p is a bound, not a value, and check_regression_batch's reported_p argument takes a float; passing 0.001 as though it were exact would test a claim the paper did not make. These rows were excluded from the 68-row batch. Their coefficients are large relative to their SEs (0.35/0.06, 0.96/0.10), so the threshold is not in doubt, but no exact verification was performed. stalt_check was not run because recovering an exact p requires the unrounded b and SE, which are not printed.

The paper reports none, so verify_power_analysis had no inputs to reproduce and was not run. This is expected for a secondary analysis of an existing trial's baseline data, where N is fixed by the parent study, but it means the adequacy of 107 participants for six multilevel SEMs with latent variable decomposition is not established anywhere in the paper.

unchecked.location: Exploratory reverse-pathway MSEMs (emotion dysregulation -> affect -> LOC eating)
unchecked.reason: Reported in the Results narrative as significant for four of six LOC dimensions, but all numeric results are in Data S1, which was not available. No coefficient, SE or p-value for these models appears in the main text or either table, so none could be checked. These analyses add a further 24 or more untested comparisons to the multiplicity picture, which the two multiplicity_report findings therefore UNDERSTATE.

Deliberately not run. Both test for baseline similarity BETWEEN randomised arms; this paper reports a single pooled sample with no arm-wise breakdown and performs no baseline comparison, so there are no baseline p-values and no group contrast to test. Running either would require inventing a grouping the paper does not report.

unchecked.location: check_effect_plausibility on the headline mediation effects
unchecked.reason: Not run. The tool benchmarks standardised mean differences (Cohen's d) against field norms; this paper's effects are within-person standardised mediation path coefficients (beta = 0.02-0.03 for indirect effects), which are not on the d scale and have no corresponding empirical benchmark in the tool's reference set. Passing them would compare incommensurable quantities.

Not applicable. GRIM-U applies only to Mann-Whitney U / Wilcoxon rank-sum p-values with stated group sizes; every p-value in this paper comes from Wald tests of multilevel SEM coefficients. Applying it here is the single most likely route to a false accusation with this tool, so it was gated out.
